subject: Mtext for ggplot2 and plotting log regression lines

messages.author: c500f0525d7f92ac
messages.subject: Mtext for ggplot2 and plotting log regression lines
parts:
Hi all,

Recently I switched from using the base graphics to ggplot2,
especially because of the nice confidence interval plotting around
regression lines. Despite all the nice graphics, I've been struggling
for a long time with the placement of text in my graph window. In the
past I have used mtext for the placement of extra information on the
graph, e.g.:
mtext(paste("Quality Standard=", selection$qstd[1]), side=3, line=0,
adj=0, cex=0.75, col="black")

However, after looking on various websites I still don't know a good
alternative for mtext in the ggplot2 package. I have tried geom_text
but then it seems to be relative to the scales and the font can't be
adjusted, and with grid.text I can't use the ggsave function. With
both of these functions it is very hard to place the text exactly
above the graph when using different scales and to have the right
alignment.

Secondly, I would like to know whether or not it is possible to plot a
regression line for a log-transformed model on a non-logtransformed
scale? So my not normally distributed data is y, the regression model
is lm(log10(y) ~ x) and I want to plot this model as well as the data
on a normal y scale (because that makes more sense to the readers).

Kind regards,
Alwin
